Definitions and address formation of current CPU pointer, current CPU variable, percpu argument wrappers, and register constraint helpers.

findings.text: Exposes width specialized per CPU operations for 1, 2, 4 and 8 byte widths covering read, write, stable read, add, bitwise and, bitwise or, exchange, add returning new value, compare exchange and boolean try compare exchange, in raw and this CPU volatility flavors, with a long alias bound to either the 8 or 4 byte read according to build variant.

Width code determines fixed unsigned carrier: code 1 uses 8 bit, code 2 uses 16 bit, code 4 uses 32 bit, code 8 uses 64 bit, and narrower inputs are reduced to the target width before use while 64 bit input passes through.
Width code determines assembler size suffix: 1 selects byte form, 2 selects word form, 4 selects long form, 8 selects quad form, applied by prefixing the supplied mnemonic.

Plain per CPU read and write have two build shapes: one dereferences the current CPU pointer with caller qualifier, the other issues a percpu addressed move through inline assembly and returns the value converted to the source type; constant read either forwards to plain read or is a compile time failure returning zero of the source type.
Stable read addresses the variable as a link time constant rather than through the current CPU variable mechanism, preserving the same width carrier and result conversion behavior.

Add helper inspects whether the increment is a compile time constant plus one or minus one and then uses increment, decrement, or generic add respectively, after a never executed assignment that checks value compatibility with the destination type.

Add returning value reports the post update contents; plain compare exchange reports the previous memory contents; boolean try compare exchange reports success and refreshes the caller supplied expected holder only on failure, with unlikely and likely hints around the failure path.
Exchange returns the prior value in both flavors: raw form performs one read followed by one write, while this CPU form reads once then retries try compare exchange in a loop until it succeeds.

Wide 64 and 128 bit compare exchange families provide raw and volatile plain and try forms; 64 bit has one shape using native 8 byte compare exchange and another shape choosing at boot between an emulation call and an 8 byte compare instruction based on processor capability, while 128 bit chooses between an emulation call and a 16 byte compare instruction based on processor capability, passing new halves in fixed registers and the variable address in another register.
Wide helpers view operands through a union that overlays the whole value with a low plus high half pair: 64 bit whole with two 32 bit halves, and 128 bit whole with two 64 bit halves.

Per CPU bit test selects by constantness of the bit number: constant index computes word offset and mask and tests the masked raw word read, variable index issues a bit test instruction and returns the observed prior bit as boolean.

Early per CPU support has a full boot variant that defines the normal per CPU object plus a boot time array initialized to the same value and a pointer to it, with declaration, export, pointer, indexed map and selector helpers that use the early array while its pointer is set and otherwise use the normal per CPU instance; a minimal variant defines only the normal object, maps early access directly to normal per CPU access, and defines the early pointer as null.

Per CPU segment addressing is abstracted so one build derives the override from the configured per CPU segment and another build leaves it empty, with a qualifier alias exposing the active choice; the viewed headers use include once guards and the perf event fragment contributes only its guard.
Some read shapes are intentionally unavailable in some builds and fail compilation if used: one constant read shape and one 8 byte stable read shape expand to a build failure rather than an access.
